shortDescription: Hypersonic flight company Stratolaunch is preparing to launch a U.S. initial public offering that could raise up to $500 million as soon as October, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday.

children: Hypersonic flight company Stratolaunch is preparing to launch a U.S. initial public offering that could raise up to $500 million as soon as October, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday.
Stratolaunch, backed by Elliott Investment Management and Cerberus Capital Management, is seeking a valuation of about $2 billion to $3 billion, the source said, adding that Goldman Sachs
The private U.S. company could make its filing public as soon as this month, said the source, who spoke on condition of anonymity as he is not authorized to speak to the media.
Stratolaunch declined to comment when contacted by Reuters.
The company operates the only autonomous, reusable, air-launched hypersonic flight test platform in the United States, which it calls the "Talon-A".

It also develops expendable hypersonic targets for missile defense testing and military training, as well as weapons subsystems for defense contractors and government customers, according to its website.
Activist investor Elliott took a stake in the company and gained board representation, the Wall Street Journal reported in January.

The Pentagon said in May 2025 Stratolaunch was part of a second successful test of a reusable hypersonic test vehicle, following an earlier test of its Talon-A vehicle in December 2024 that was not publicized.
